newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW - Posadas eyes Situr hotels.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Posadas eyes Situr hotels.

text.p: Grupo Posadas, Mexico's largest hotel chain, is interested in buying hotel properties from troubled tourism firm Grupo Situr, according to Posadas' assistant director general Genaro Marquez.

"The sale of Situr's properties is something we are aware of and are following with great interest ... when Situr does carry out these operations, we'll be there," Marquez told Reuters in an interview.
Situr, which defaulted on its debt earlier this year, plans to sell assets as part of its restructuring efforts.
Mrquez said Posadas' interest in Situr's properties depends on the eventual agreements the tourism firm reaches with its creditor banks.

"(Our interest) depends on the restructuring process...we will make our best effort to obtain those properties that interest us by offering bids according to market conditions and income potential," Mrquez said. He added interest in individual Situr hotels depends on whether or not they fit the concept of Posadas' two main hotel chains, Fiesta Americana and Fiesta Inn.
The executive said Posadas is financially healthy enough following its own recent restructuring to finance expansion plans.
Posadas obtained a $70.2 million credit on June 18 to strengthen its balance sheet, consisting mostly of a $50.2 million credit from the International Finance Corp.
A recent Eurobond issue also netted the company $20 million, which it used to buy a stake in a real estate fund venture with U.S. investment bank Morgan Stanley.
Mrquez said the fund, which has $200 million at its disposal, has not made any purchases, but is looking into several options.
